content: Rifampin increases the metabolism of carvedilol, leading to reduced levels of the drug. Exercise caution and monitor the patient closely. Rifampin increases the metabolism of caspofungin, resulting in decreased drug levels. Use caution and monitor the patient. Cenobamate reduces the levels or effects of rifampin by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Increase the dose of CYP2B6 substrates as needed when co-administered with cenobamate. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cevimeline by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of chlordiazepoxide by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of chloroquine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin increases the toxicity of cholic acid by reducing its elimination. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Avoid the concurrent use of bile salt efflux pump (BSEP) inhibitors, as this may exacerbate the accumulation of conjugated bile salts in the liver, potentially leading to clinical symptoms. If co-administration is unavoidable, monitor serum transaminases and bilirubin levels. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of citalopram by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clarithromycin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clomipramine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clonazepam by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of clorazepate by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Clotrimazole increases the levels or effects of rifampin through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Co-administration with cotrimoxazole increases rifampin concentrations, which may elevate the risk of toxicity. Monitor for adverse reactions during co-administration. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of clozapine by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of conjugated estrogens by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of vaginal conjugated estrogens by influencing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cortisone by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels of crizotinib by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Crizotinib increases rifampin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of cyclophosphamide by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of cyclosporine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Danicopan increases the levels or effects of rifampin by influencing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Danicopan also increases plasma concentrations of P-gp substrates; consider reducing the dose of P-gp substrates where minimal concentration changes may lead to serious adverse reactions. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dantrolene by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daprodustat through other mechanisms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. CYP2C8 inducers may reduce daprodustat exposure, potentially leading to a loss of efficacy. Monitor hemoglobin levels and adjust the daprodustat dose when initiating or discontinuing CYP2C8 inducers during treatment. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dapsone by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of daunorubicin by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels of deferasirox through other mechanisms. Use caution and monitor the patient. Avoid the concurrent use of potent UGT inducers with deferasirox. If co-administration is necessary, consider increasing the initial dose of deferasirox to 30 mg/kg and monitor ferritin levels and clinical response. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of deflazacort by influencing the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dexamethasone by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dexlansoprazole by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of diazepam (buccal) by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the rate of diazepam elimination, potentially reducing its efficacy. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of diazepam (intranasal) by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C19 metabolism and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inducers may increase the rate of diazepam elimination, potentially reducing its efficacy. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of digoxin by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter and increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of disopyramide by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of docetaxel by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dolutegravir by increasing its metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Increase the dolutegravir dosage when co-administering with strong UGT1A/CYP3A4 inducers. Consider using an alternative to rifampin in patients with integrase strand transfer inhibitor (INSTI)-associated resistance substitutions or suspected INSTI resistance, as concomitant use may result in therapeutic failure and resistance development. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of donepezil by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxepin cream by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of doxorubicin by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of doxorubicin liposomal by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of dronabinol by influencing hepatic enzyme CYP2C9/10 metabolism and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Dronabinol is a CYP3A4 substrate. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of dutasteride by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of duvelisib by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of efavirenz by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin reduces the levels or effects of elafibranor by increasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor the patient. Rifampin increases the levels or effects of elagolix through other mechanisms. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is necessary. Elagolix increases rifampin levels by affecting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Rifampin decreases the levels or effects of elagolix by influencing hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the concomitant use of elagolix 150 mg daily and rifampin to six months.
